name: Demo · Medical device · CRD-07 (pivotal)
description: Implanted device. SAEs and device deficiencies within 3 calendar days; only trained, listed implanters; serial numbers tracked.

topics.major: SAE follow-up report overdue; PI causality not documented
topics.critical: SAE unreported, or reported outside 24 hours (stays critical even with a CAPA)

topics.major: AEs missing from EDC or not graded. (The PI not assessing AEs is PI_OVERSIGHT, a separate problem.)

topics.minor: missing time of signature; initials missing on a page
topics.major: outdated ICF version used (major even if the subject was re-consented during the visit); re-consent overdue
topics.critical: study procedures before consent; no signed ICF

topics.minor: eligibility checklist unsigned but criteria met
topics.major: eligibility evidence missing from source at randomization
topics.critical: ineligible subject randomized or dosed. Only report eligibility when a subject's eligibility is actually in doubt or undocumented; how eligibility questions get answered (e.g. by email from an absent PI) is PI_OVERSIGHT

topics.display: Safety reports to IRB and PI
topics.minor: IND safety reports filed late in the ISF
topics.major: safety reports not reviewed by the PI or not sent to the IRB
blinded staff could see unblinded documents, no unblinding

topics.minor: a single out-of-window visit or assessment (including one rescheduled outside its window)
topics.major: important deviations; safety assessments missed entirely (not just late); deviations not logged
missed doses undocumented; compliance not reconciled (including returned doses not counted)
topics.critical: wrong dose, double dose, or dosed despite a hold criterion

topics.minor: small count difference explained on site
topics.major: kits unaccounted for; wrong kit dispensed

topics.minor: brief excursion with no product impact, reported; or an excursion that was reported with the product quarantined and not used while the Sponsor decides
topics.major: excursion not reported; logs not kept
topics.critical: product used after an excursion before Sponsor assessment

topics.major: samples mishandled or not shipped; central lab results not reviewed

topics.minor: a few pages or one concomitant medication not entered
topics.major: backlog older than 60 days, or a large volume (about 25 or more pages not entered)
many queries open more than 60 days, or 10 or more queries older than 30 days
SDV far behind; the monitor's EMR access lapsed
topics.critical: the site refuses access to source documents

topics.major: source missing or contradicts EDC; ALCOA+ failures

topics.minor: one CV or GCP certificate expired; training still to be completed before the person starts study work
topics.major: staff not on the delegation log who are not yet doing study work; turnover with no backup
topics.critical: staff already performing study procedures or running visits without delegation or training

topics.major: PI not signing labs or eCRFs (a backlog or a long delay); PI not assessing AEs (causality or grade); PI unavailable to the team. A routine request for the PI to sign items before the next contact is an action item, not a finding
far behind target
missing 1572, amendment approval or licenses; a pending IRB approval that blocks screening
equipment out of calibration; lab certification (CLIA/CAP) expired
prior actions not done; CAPA not implemented
unresponsive for weeks; repeated visit cancellations

study_rules: An implant performed by a physician who is not trained and listed is an important protocol deviation. [STAFF_TURNOVER, critical if broken] (protocol CRD-07 Revision C, p. 2)
The serial number of every device received, implanted, explanted or returned must be recorded in the device accountability log. [IP_ACCOUNTABILITY, major if broken] (protocol CRD-07 Revision C, p. 3)
Follow-up visits take place at 3, 6 and 12 months after implant, each within plus or minus 14 days. [PROTOCOL_DEVIATION, minor if broken] (protocol CRD-07 Revision C, p. 4)

Serious adverse events and device deficiencies that could have led to a serious adverse event must be reported to the sponsor within 3 calendar days of the site becoming aware of them. [SAE_REPORTING, critical if broken] (protocol CRD-07 Revision C, p. 5)

deadlines.what: Serious adverse events and device deficiencies that could have led to a serious adverse event must be reported to the sponsor within 3 calendar days of the site becoming aware of them.
